claim: A theory in neuroscience under the pragmatic view is a set of assumptions instantiated in models, vetted via experimentation, with a well-established translation function connecting them to phenomena; it is a continuously developing body of canonical models and model-phenomenon correspondences.
falsifier: One can test this by examining whether theories in neuroscience fit this characterization when analyzed according to the pragmatic view.

conditions: Under the pragmatic view of theory in neuroscience
exclusions: Limited to the pragmatic view as described in the reviewed literature; other views of theory may differ.

title: Theories in neuroscience–Characterization of a theory theorem

claim: In restrained molecular dynamics simulations, a small fraction of pairwise distance restraints (less than 2% of residue pairs) can induce conformational changes between distinct states of a protein when the target state is a local minimum of the force field.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by performing restrained MD simulations on a protein with two known conformations, selecting restraints using the largest change in pairwise separation method with Nr/N ≈ 0.02, and measuring whether the simulation converges to the target structure with RMSD below a reference value.

conditions: protein has two distinct conformational states
target state is a local minimum of the force field (e.g., in vitro structures for T4L, PGK, AK)
restraints selected using optimal method (largest change in pairwise separation)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported proteins (T4L, PGK, AK) and the AMBER99SB-ILDN force field; transfer to other proteins or force fields is unestablished.

claim: Deposition of graphene via chemical vapor deposition (CVD) on copper films increases the in-plane thermal conductivity and thermal diffusivity near room temperature, with the enhancement being more pronounced for thinner films.
falsifier: Repeat the experiment with Cu films of different thicknesses under identical CVD conditions and measure thermal conductivity and diffusivity using the same in-plane measurement technique.

conditions: film thickness of 9 μm or 25 μm
single-layer graphene (SLG) or few-layer graphene (FLG) deposited by CVD
exclusions: limited to the reported Cu film thicknesses (9 μm and 25 μm) and deposition conditions; transfer to other thicknesses or materials is unestablished

title: Deposition of graphene via–in-plane thermal conductivity principle
